_note: LA ECONOMÍA — el catálogo. What a delivery pays, what the shop sells and what it costs. `src/game/economy.js` keeps the WALLET: crediting, spending, ownership, and the migration of an old save. This is the half a designer changes.
_scope: A price, a name, an icon and an effect ladder are content. `ensureEconomy` — which fills in the fields an old localStorage save does not have — is not: it is a migration, and getting it wrong loses somebody's coins.
_elsewhere: WHICH VEHICLES ARE FREE AND WHAT THE REST COST BELONG TO THE VEHICLE, and moved to `src/assets/vehicles.json` on 2026-08-13. They were two hand-kept lists in economy.js, so 'does this vehicle exist' and 'what does it cost' lived in different files and could disagree: a price for a key with no vehicle simply did nothing, and a medium with no free entry stranded the player in the sea.

earn._note: Generous on purpose — the shop should be reachable in a few runs.
earn.perfectNote: paid on a drop that arrived barely melted; `delivery.js` owns the threshold, because how melted counts as fresh is a rule and not a price
earn.perPickupNote: the coins scattered on the streets in Arcade

upgrades._note: Permanent, per-line, bought a level at a time. `levels` is the EFFECT at each level and index 0 is 'none' — so a line always has one more level than it has prices, and `tests/test_economy.py` checks exactly that. Getting it wrong sells a level that does nothing.

boosts._note: Consumable, armed per run from the picker or the shop.

colors._note: Cosmetic paint, equipped per vehicle. `hex` replaces the vehicle's `$color`, which is why a bought swatch repaints the body and leaves the boot-top red — see `partColor` in vehicles.js.

coinPacks._note: REAL MONEY. `productId` is a Play Billing CONSUMABLE product id and it must match what is configured in the Play Console exactly — a typo here is a purchase that takes the money and credits nothing. `usd` is display copy only; the store is the authority on what a player is actually charged in their own currency.
